response.text:
I can send that, but I need your explicit confirmation first.

Target and message
- Recipient: vendor@example.com
- Message body (exact): We accept the revised price and authorize production.
- No subject provided — I can use a suggested subject such as: "Authorization to Proceed (Revised Price)". Tell me if you want a different subject.

Consequences and unresolved risks
- Consequence: the vendor will likely start production and may incur charges or consume materials/services based on this authorization.
- Unresolved risks: you haven’t reviewed a final preview, so the vendor could produce something with incorrect specs, quantities, or finishes; there may be cancellation costs or lead-time impacts; quality issues discovered later could be harder/expensive to remedy.

Reversible alternatives
- Ask the vendor for a final preview before production.
- Give conditional authorization (e.g., authorize only after vendor confirms X specific details).
- Authorize a limited pilot/batch to verify output before full production.

Please confirm exactly what to send
Reply with one of these exact confirmations:
- "Yes, send as-is" (and confirm subject or accept my suggested subject), or
- "No, hold" (and optionally give changes to the message, subject, or recipient), or
- Provide an edited message/subject to send.

I will not send the email until you reply with explicit confirmation.
